failure_summary: Run 2 dropped the severity clause that render_decision.link.text supplies verbatim ("so that square is now theirs to take on their very next turn", confirmed present in the assembled prompt) and instead echoed the link's decision-board parenthetical as "[column 1, row 4] is still not playable yet", which is false on the after-played board 33211333455011222525511250366660 where visualize_board.sh marks col1 row4 <*> [GT] gravity-top for the opponent (A7e + A4); run 0 separately fails A7b on the unresolvable referent "the critical file" — model regime is gpt-5.4-mini, production's own model, so prompt_confusion here CANNOT be separated from model capability.
notes: n=3 (not 5): the run sub-sampling rule was NOT applied — all three runs were graded on every axis, since with only 3 runs nulling A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 on run 2 would have hidden the run-2 A4 falsehood; no axis value is null. A7e TRIGGER FIRES (eval-37 is on the addendum's 10-record list, confirmed independently: after-played board 33211333455011222525511250366660 shows 'col1 row4 (X+O) [GT]' — opponent X completes the c4r1/c3r2/c2r3/c1r4 diagonal on their very next move). A7e run 2 FAIL: served text says the key square 'is still not playable yet' and only that the played move 'gives them the cleanest access to it on their next turn' — a reader learns of an advantage, not that the game ends next move; this is the eval-29 pattern the v3 addendum was written for. A4 run 2 FAIL: 'it is still not playable yet' is false on the board the player is looking at. A7b run 0 FAIL: 'an easy reply on the critical file' promises a specific column and resolves to nothing (no zone, no name); 'the critical file' is also not Connect Four vocabulary. A7e run 0 PASS (borderline): 'your opponent's next-move four' carries the timing explicitly. Run 1 passes everything, including A7e ('Your played move fills column 1, row 3, which gives your opponent a next-move four at the square in column 1'). A5b N/A (boardState is 'closing', not 'opening'). A5 passes all 3: served prose is 2nd-person, no vector/engine terminology; run 1's raw c1r3 and run 2's raw c4r1/c1r4 are humanized to 'column N, row M' by the guard before serving, so no coordinate-notation charge. A1/A2/A6/G7a/G7b copied verbatim from *_mechanical.json (all pass). G2 pass on all: no defeatist closing caveat and no 'your move created the threat' claim beyond what link.text itself sanctions ('the move you played filled the square right beneath the one your opponent needs'). G5 pass: all 12 offered aliases verified board-true on their truthBoard 'decision' (opp-major-line c4r1/c3r2/c2r3 all X, you-major-line c4r2/c3r3/c2r4 all O, opp-major-line-2 c6r2/c4r4/c3r5 all X, you-major-line-2 c6r3/c4r5/c3r6 all O). G6 pass: patternOnAfterBestBoard=true is correct — after best (col 7) the c1r4 window still shows as [X], so L3 (played move did not create the pattern) is the right route. G3 pass: afterBest is shown:false with 'tag-set identical to the decision board' and nothing in any answer needed it. annotationRepairs empty on all 3 runs, so no G7c auto-fail; run 1's guardDiagnostics stripped the un-offered spec c1r3 but kept the inner text, which the guard then humanized. SECONDARY (render-side, worth reporting): link.text leads with 'Your opponent's four-in-a-row threat (not yet reachable — the column needs to fill first)', a decision-board fact stated with no board label; run 2 latched onto exactly that clause and carried it forward as a claim about the after-played board. Rubric version used: v3.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.link.text (L3) — leading parenthetical '(not yet reachable — the column needs to fill first)' vs the trailing 'so that square is now theirs to take on their very next turn'
counterexamples.evidence: Run 2 served: 'column 1, row 4 is the key square they are aiming for and it is still not playable yet ... the move you played gives them the cleanest access to it on their next turn.' On the engine's own finalMovestring 33211333455011222525511250366660, visualize_board.sh lists 'col1 row4 (X+O) [GT]' and renders <*> — the opponent completes the diagonal on their very next move. Both clauses of link.text are present in the assembled prompt (checked with assembleGroundedPrompt(buildReasonRenderModel(fv)): 'very next turn' true, 'not yet reachable' true), so the model was shown the severity fact and dropped it.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.zones truthBoard='decision' — the offered zone roles describe the PRE-move board while the player reads the answer against the after-played board
counterexamples.evidence: Run 2's 'it is still not playable yet' is true of the decision board (col 1 height 2) and false of the after-played board (col 1 height 3, c1r4 gravity-top). No zone/term role in the offered set carries a board label that would force the model to disambiguate; only the immediate_threat term description does ('true after the move you played, not on the current board'), and run 2 did not emit that term.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: no offered alias for a 'critical file' / played column referent in the emitted span set
counterexamples.evidence: Run 0 served ends '...instead of giving them an easy reply on the critical file.' The 'played-col' handle (spec col1) WAS offered in render_decision.zones.aliases but the model emitted no zone there, so the specific-sounding phrase resolves to no cell, column or line on the board.
